solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Invoice company directors for large sign

blocks.note: An invoice is a bill for goods or work
A company's directors sit together as its board

explanation.surface: Someone is sending the directors a bill for putting up a big sign.
explanation.walkthrough: The two business words simply join: BILL then BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A billboard is the huge outdoor hoarding that carries advertising posters beside roads.

clue.text: Resist horned creature

blocks.note: A verb for going against something, as a trend or the system
A male deer, which carries antlers

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses of the same word sit side by side with nothing joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to oppose or go against; the noun is a male deer or antelope.

clue.text: Spy novelist appears back inside terrace lodgings

indicators.note: Reading back means the run of letters is taken from right to left
The answer sits inside the phrase terrace lodgings, spanning both words

blocks.note: The letters straddling the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A thriller writer's name is spotted in a row of terraced digs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read tERRACE Lodgings from right to left to find LE CARRE.
explanation.definitionFit: John le Carré wrote Cold War espionage thrillers such as Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy.

clue.text: Throw away part of pen that’s used up

indicators.note: In a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: The writing tip of a fountain pen

explanation.surface: Chucking out a worn-out bit of an old pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Used up looks like exhausted, but in a down clue up turns NIB into BIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To bin something is the informal British verb for discarding it as rubbish.

clue.text: Painter, say, with odd traits

indicators.note: Odd suggests the letters of traits are in a strange order

blocks.note: Used as it stands

explanation.surface: The eccentric painter stereotype: a creative type with strange habits.
explanation.walkthrough: Say marks the painter as one example of the answer, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is one kind of creative person working in the visual arts.

clue.text: Rowdy crowd hoot for sci-fi show

indicators.note: Rowdy suggests the letters of crowd hoot are unruly and scrambled

blocks.note: Both words used as they stand

explanation.surface: A noisy audience jeering at a science-fiction programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowdy reads as describing the crowd, but it is telling you to scramble the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-running BBC television series about a time-travelling alien in a police box.

clue.text: Pastry’s price displayed regularly

indicators.note: Regularly means every other letter of price is shown

blocks.note: First, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A bakery's price tag for a pastry, shown on the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s reads as a possessive but stands for is, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish with a crust made of pastry, so the words overlap loosely.

clue.text: Wheeze carrying one material for decorating

indicators.note: To carry is to hold, so wheeze holds one

blocks.note: To wheeze is to breathe hard
The Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wheezy decorator hauling a tin of material up the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: Wheeze could be a scheme, but here it is breathing: PANT with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint is the coloured liquid spread on walls when doing up a room.

clue.text: Blow up general, unfortunately

indicators.note: Unfortunately suggests general has gone wrong and is jumbled

blocks.note: Used as it stands

explanation.surface: A regrettable explosion that kills a military general.
explanation.walkthrough: Blow up suggests explosions, but the definition means make bigger, as with a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a picture is to make a larger print of it, which is the verb here.

clue.text: Chanel, say, fanatic for tropical fruit

blocks.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer
A nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A devoted fashion fan swaps couture for exotic produce.
explanation.walkthrough: Say shows Chanel is an example of someone named COCO.
explanation.definitionFit: The coconut is the large hard-shelled seed of a palm grown in hot climates.

clue.text: Relax, beginning to climb high ground

indicators.note: The beginning of climb means only its opening letter is taken

blocks.note: Opening letter
A hill is raised ground

explanation.surface: Taking a breather as you start the ascent of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma separates the definition; the rest builds C plus HILL.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill is slang for unwinding and taking it easy.

clue.text: Coaches ceramicist, one with a track record?

blocks.note: To coach someone is to train them
A ceramicist makes pots

explanation.surface: A sports coach who also makes pottery, with a proven history of success.
explanation.walkthrough: Coaches looks like a noun (buses or carriages) but is the verb. The question mark flags the pun: a track here is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A British railway hobbyist logs locomotive numbers seen, keeping written notes on the railway lines.

clue.text: I am someone in hospital, possibly fidgety

blocks.note: I am shortened to I'm
A person receiving hospital treatment

explanation.surface: A hospital inmate confessing to restlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pun: patient in the ward yet anything but patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone restless and unwilling to wait tends to twitch and shift about in their seat.

clue.text: Drowsy Yankee strips in reverse?

indicators.note: In reverse tells you to read Yankee and strips backwards together

blocks.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
To strip the skin off fruit is to peel it

explanation.surface: A tired American undressing slowly, perhaps backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Strips reads as undressing but means peels; the whole Y plus PEELS string is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone heavy-eyed and ready for bed.

clue.text: One studying larch so haphazardly

indicators.note: Haphazardly means without order, so larch and so are rearranged

blocks.note: Both words used as they stand

explanation.surface: A botanist making a rather careless study of a larch tree.
explanation.walkthrough: One studying is a noun phrase, the person who studies, matching the noun answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or student devoted to academic learning.

clue.text: Suddenly turn west, interrupting start of rally?

indicators.note: To interrupt is to break into, so west breaks into start of rally

blocks.note: The compass abbreviation
In tennis every rally begins with a serve

explanation.surface: A rally driver veering west just after the start of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: Start of rally looks like an instruction to take R; the question mark signals it is the tennis stroke instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve is to veer abruptly off one's line, as a car avoiding an obstacle.

clue.text: Italian dish — it’s roots in a stew

indicators.note: In a stew means agitated and mixed up, so the letters are stirred

blocks.note: Used as it stands
Used as it stands

explanation.surface: A recipe note: this Italian dish is root vegetables cooked in a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for has, joining it to roots; the misspelling of its is deliberate to make the surface read.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a rice dish from northern Italy cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Turn away, taking in opening of drink commercial

indicators.note: Taking in means turn away holds the opening of drink inside it
The opening of drink means only its first letter is used

blocks.note: To avert your eyes is to turn them away
First letter

explanation.surface: Someone turning away from a drinks commercial on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Drink commercial reads as one phrase, but the definition is commercial alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is the British short form for an advertisement, such as a TV ad break spot.

clue.text: Use handout he developed for spooky location

indicators.note: Developed suggests the words have been worked into a new form

blocks.note: All three words used as they stand

explanation.surface: A man produces a leaflet to advertise a creepy venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Handout looks like a single meaningful noun; it is just fodder along with use and he.
explanation.definitionFit: A building said to be visited by ghosts is the classic eerie place of ghost stories.

clue.text: Female relative not initially let loose?

indicators.note: Not initially means the first letter of female relative is dropped

blocks.note: An aunt, informally

explanation.surface: A female relative who at first was not allowed to run free.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE loses its A to give UNTIE; the question mark allows the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo knots or bonds is to free something that was tied down or held.

clue.text: Golf club missing top and side

indicators.note: In a down clue the top is the first letter, which golf club loses

blocks.note: A lofted iron for short shots

explanation.surface: A damaged golf club with its head and one side broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: WEDGE loses its W. Golf club might suggest a clubhouse; it is the stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of something is its outer border or boundary, a flank.

clue.text: Coffee seen in the middle of platter

indicators.note: The answer is seen within the inner letters of platter

blocks.note: Drop the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cup of coffee placed at the centre of a serving tray.
explanation.walkthrough: pLATTEr: the answer is the inside of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink topped up with lots of steamed milk.

clue.text: Thrilled former partner gets referenced

blocks.note: An ex is a former spouse or lover
To cite a source is to reference it

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to be mentioned by their former partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Gets simply joins the two pieces, EX followed by CITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone full of eager delight and enthusiasm.

clue.text: River starts to curve around mountain

indicators.note: Starts means the first letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: Initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A river beginning to bend its way round a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Cam flows through Cambridge, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cam is an English river, famous for punting past the Cambridge colleges.

clue.text: Regret street in Paris

blocks.note: A literary verb for feeling sorry about something done
The French word for street

explanation.walkthrough: One English verb and one French noun that happen to be spelt alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to feel sorrow over; the French noun names a road in a town.

clue.text: To short-term worker, cry of appreciation for carving

blocks.note: Used as it stands
A temp is a temporary employee
The Spanish shout of approval, as at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Cheering a temporary office worker for their sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: Short-term looks like it might mean abbreviate something; it is just part of the phrase for a temp.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall wooden post carved with figures, made by peoples of the Pacific Northwest.
